sanskrit: abhi tvā śatapāśayā- -atho sahasrapāśayā | dāśo matsyam iva tīdena mayi badhnāmi te manaḥ ||
english: With a hundred nooses and with a thousand nooses I bind your mind to me, as a fisherman binds a fish with his net.

sanskrit: ā hi te dakṣiṇaṃ padaṃ hṛdayyaṃ dade | upasthe padamopi ni tvām akri sve vaśe ||
english: I have taken your right foot, your heart. I have placed your foot in my lap — I have made you subject to my will.

sanskrit: pari tvā gām ivāsaraṃ mama patto nipattave | tan mārutaṃ ha vairudham āvataṃkaraṇaṃ kṛtam ||
english: Like a cow that has been tethered, I cause you to fall at my feet. That wind-charm, that binding-spell — it has been made to draw you in.

sanskrit: ā nayāmi te mano aśvam ivāśvābhidhānyā | upa te muñce manaḥ pador upānahau yathā ||
english: I lead your mind as a horse-tether leads a horse. I bind your mind to you as sandals are bound to the feet.

sanskrit: yathā surā yathā madhu yathākṣā adhidevane | yathā ha gavyato mana evā mām abhi te manaḥ ||
english: As surā (beer), as honey, as dice drawn to the gaming-board, as the mind of one longing for cattle — so let your mind turn toward me.

sanskrit: evā kṛṇuṣva mā priyām antaḥ kṛṇuṣva mā hṛdi | yathā mannāpacetayā nānyāsāṃ kīrtayāś cana ||
english: So make me your beloved; place me within your heart; so that, your mind undivided, you will not even speak of other women.

sanskrit: yasyedaṃ vaiṣṭapaṃ havir bhagasya hastayor hitam | tenā tvābhi mṛśāmasi saubhāgyāya svastaye ||
english: With this vaiṣṭapa oblation placed in the hands of Bhaga, we touch you — for good fortune and for well-being.

sanskrit: bhaga memāṃ saṃ baṭ karo mā paścān mā paro daghaḥ | adhā bhagasya yo bhagas tenemāṃ saṃ sṛjā bhaga ||
english: O Bhaga, unite me with her! Do not scorch her from behind or from beyond. And with that fortune which is Bhaga's own fortune, unite me with her, O Bhaga!

sanskrit: bhagena tvā saṃ sṛjāmi māsureṇa surām iva | yathāsasi priyā patyur devṛbhyaḥ subhagāsasi ||
english: I unite you with Bhaga as the month unites with surā — so that you may be dear to your husband and favored by your brothers-in-law.

sanskrit: ud ito daivyaṃ vaca iṣum iva tunnaḥ khide | tenā sapatnān māmakān sāsahāni jahāni ca ||
english: From here rises the divine word, shot like an arrow into the quiver. With it I shall conquer and drive away my rivals.

sanskrit: agnir mā pātu vasubhiḥ purastāt savitādityair abhi pātu dakṣiṇāt | indro marudbhir abhi pātu paścād viśve devā abhi rakṣantu mottarāt ||
english: May Agni with the Vasus protect me from the east; may Savitṛ with the Ādityas protect me from the south; may Indra with the Maruts protect me from the west; may all the gods guard me from the north.

sanskrit: devarakṣasān mā pāhi manuṣyarakṣasān mā pāhi | viśvasmān mā rakṣasas pāhi ||
english: Protect me from the demon-rākṣasas; protect me from the human-rākṣasas; protect me from every rākṣasa.

sanskrit: asau yas trikakud giriḥ śṛṅgābhyām abhitiṣṭhati | sa saṃpatatram udyugaṃ balāsam iva tiṣṭhatu ||
english: That mountain yonder, the three-peaked one, which stands firm with its two horns — let it stand holding the swooping-winged, the upward-rushing one, as it holds balāsa disease.

sanskrit: divyaḥ suparṇa ā patad ayodaṃṣṭro ayomukhaḥ | sa saṃpatatram udyugam ito yakṣmaṃ parā bhavat ||
english: The celestial Suparṇa (eagle) flies down, iron-fanged, iron-beaked. Let it drive away from here the swooping, the upward-rushing wasting disease.

sanskrit: sākaṃ balāsa pra pata cāṣeṇa kikidīvyā | sākaṃ vātasya dhrājyā saha naśya nihākayā ||
english: Fly away together, O balāsa, with the jay and the kikidī bird; perish together with the rushing of the wind and with the nihākā.

sanskrit: mābhi gāyaḥ śābaleyaṃ śauṇeyaṃ sādhuvāhinam | namas te bhadrayā kṛṇmo 'vihvṛtā cakṣuṣā tvaṃ śamakā śamayāti tvā ||
english: Do not sing at the śābalī hound, the śauṇeya that draws well. We render homage to you with a good offering. With an undistracted eye — you, O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.

sanskrit: tṛndhi vi kṣiṇīhi peśaḥ kurvāṇikā tvam | jāreṇa patyā jakṣatī gṛhān gopāyamānikā śamakā śamayāti tvā ||
english: You who disfigure, who diminish beauty — you who devour together with a paramour as husband, guarding the house — O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.

sanskrit: āṅkṣvābhyaṅkṣva- -abhyaktā śamanaṃ gamaḥ | atho pitṛbhyo gā iccha vijñānena bhagena ca śamakā śamayāti tvā ||
english: Anoint yourself, smear yourself well — when anointed go to the calming. And seek cows for the ancestors with knowledge and with Bhaga. O śamakā, let śamayā calm you.

sanskrit: apehi manasas pāpa- -apa krāma parastaram | paro nirṛtyā ā cakṣur bahutrā jīvato manaḥ ||
english: Go away, O evil of the mind; step further away! Beyond Nirṛti the eye looks out — the mind of the living is in many places.

sanskrit: bhadraṃ vai varaṃ vṛṇate bhadraṃ yuñjanti dakṣiṇam | bhadraṃ vaivasvataṃ cakṣur bahutrā jīvato manaḥ ||
english: They choose the auspicious boon; they yoke the auspicious dakṣiṇā; the eye of Vaivasvata is auspicious — the mind of the living is in many places.

sanskrit: yan me chidraṃ manaso yac ca vācaḥ sarasvatīṃ manyucittaṃ jagāma | viśvais tad devaiḥ saha saṃvidānaḥ saṃ dadhātu bṛhaspatiḥ ||
english: Whatever flaw is in my mind and in my speech — whatever went to Sarasvatī driven by anger of thought — may Bṛhaspati, in accord with all the gods, bind that together again.

sanskrit: sphirā sphirataraṃ sphirā āttāraḥ | śatahasta samāhara sahasrahasta saṃ kira ||
english: Thrive, thrive more greatly — thrive, O receivers! O hundred-handed one, gather in; O thousand-handed one, pour in abundantly.

sanskrit: ihaivā kira saṃ kira- -ihaiva sphātim asphiram | sphireyam astv oṣadhiḥ samudrasyeva saṃsravaḥ ||
english: Pour it in right here, pour it all in right here — let there be thriving in this place. Let this herb be prosperous, like the confluence of the ocean.

sanskrit: ut tirā ā gamann upa- -ut tirāṇyāgaman | vṛṣṭe śāpaṃ nadīr iva- -iha sphātiṃ samāvahān ||
english: The tīrā plants have come up and gathered close; the great tīrā plants have arrived. As rivers after rain bring abundance here — let them bring thriving hither.

sanskrit: vi mayūkhā ā yacchantu gardabhā iva duryujaḥ | muhyantu sarve tantavo vṛtā nāḍī vitantrike ||
english: Let the pegs spread apart, like donkeys hard to yoke. Let all the threads become confused — the nāḍī tube wrapped around the loom-frame.

sanskrit: pra vām īṣve patatāṃ pra taṭā pra niveṣṭanam | muhyantu sarve tantavo andhe vitatavāyyau ||
english: Let the shuttles fall forward; let the banks and the winding-spool fall forward. Let all the threads become confused in the blind stretched warp-yarn.

sanskrit: āyavanī niveṣṭanaṃ vratā tasaram īṣve | muhyantu sarve tantavo andhe vitata vāyyau ||
english: The āyavanī rod, the winding-spool, the pattern-stick, the spool, the shuttles — let all the threads become confused in the blind, stretched warp-yarn.

sanskrit: mayārakārī prathamā- -ūrṇavābhir atho śakā | devānāṃ patnīḥ kṛttikā imaṃ tantum amūmuhan ||
english: She who first makes the peacock-pattern — together with the spider and with śakā — the Kṛttikās, wives of the gods, have confused this thread.

sanskrit: agnir na etu prathamaḥ puraetā bṛhaspatiḥ | adhā bhaga pra ṇo yaccha tvaṃ hi dhanadā asi ||
english: Let Agni go first; let Bṛhaspati go before us. And then, O Bhaga, grant us your boon — for you are the giver of wealth.

sanskrit: pra ṇaḥ śūdra utāryaḥ pra ṇo rājota vṛtrahā | atho yat sarvam ātmanvat pra ṇo yacchatu dakṣiṇām ||
english: May the śūdra and the ārya grant us bounty; may the king, even Vṛtrahā (Indra), grant us bounty; and may everything that has a self grant us the dakṣiṇā reward.

sanskrit: kavir yajñasya vi tanoṣi panthām ṛtasya pṛṣṭhe adhi dīdhyānaḥ | yena havyaṃ vahasi deva dūta itaḥ pracetā amuto vanīyān ||
english: O seer, you stretch out the path of the sacrifice, shining upon the back of Ṛta. By which path you carry the oblation, O divine messenger — may the wise one be more glorious from here than from there.

sanskrit: madhuhasto madhujihvo madhuvarṇo madhuvrataḥ | atho madhupraśāsano bhago mā varcasāvatu ||
english: Honey-handed, honey-tongued, honey-complexioned, honey-vowed, and honey-commanding — may Bhaga enrich me with radiance.

sanskrit: yā triṣaptaiḥ punar eti nānā rūpāṇi bibhratī | vācaspatir balā tasyā āre hetiṃ dadhātu mat ||
english: She who returns again three times seven, wearing many forms — may Vācaspati place the force of her weapon far away from me.

sanskrit: vācā nuttā kṛtyād indravatī jāgratā svapatī kṛtā | nuttā pākasya śaṃsena pratyak kartāram ṛcchatu ||
english: Driven back by the word from the kṛtyā, endowed with Indra's power, made to stay awake though asleep — driven back by the declaration of the simple one, let it turn back and strike the maker.

sanskrit: yad etad bhūri spardhase kṛtyāsmīti manyase | pratīcīnā paretya viṣād iva viṣamad dhataḥ ||
english: Inasmuch as you boast greatly and think 'I am the kṛtyā' — turning back and departing, you shall be slain like poison by poison.

sanskrit: pareṇaitv aghaśaṃso mainena sam arāmahi | dyauś cāsmān pṛthivī ca- -ubhe pātām aṃhasaḥ ||
english: Let the evil-proclaiming one pass beyond; let us not come together with him. May both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress.

sanskrit: yava yāvayāsmad dveṣāṃsi yavamayena haviṣā | durhārde cakruṣe kṛtyāṃ grīvāsu prati muñcatam ||
english: O barley, drive away from us all hatreds with the barley oblation. Upon the neck of the one who has worked the kṛtyā with malevolent heart — release it back upon him.

sanskrit: anyā vo anyām avatv anyānyasyā upāvata | aśvā iva pravalgantīḥ kṛtyāṃ hatauṣadhayo 'rātiṃ hatauṣadhayaḥ ||
english: Let one of you assist another; let each help the other. Like horses galloping forward — the plants that slay the kṛtyā, the plants that slay hostility.

sanskrit: mehopa gā mopa raṃsthāḥ pathāṃ durgāṇy anv ihi | sapatni naśyatād ito dūraṃ gacchādhy okasaḥ ||
english: Go not near the cattle, do not linger near them; follow the difficult passes of the roads. Let the rival wife perish from here; let her go far away from her home.

sanskrit: yasyās te nāma gṛhnāmi yasminn āramasecane | ā parasyāḥ parāvataḥ sapatnīṃ nāśayāmasi ||
english: Whose name I take up, in whom the resting-and-pouring-in abides — from that far-off distance of the remote one, we cause the rival wife to be destroyed.

sanskrit: triṃśataṃ trīṃś ca parvatāṃś caturaś ca girīn ati | sapatnīṃ brahmaṇaspate paro bhrūṇāny arpayā ||
english: Beyond thirty-three mountains and beyond four hills — O Brahmaṇaspati, drive the rival wife away, along with her embryos.

sanskrit: un mādayata marutaḥ samudriyā ud dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe | ut tvā samudra ṛṣantu- -ut tvām agnir ayaṃ dahāt ||
english: Let the sea-faring Maruts exhilarate upward; let both Heaven and Earth rise up. Let the ocean's floods rush up against you; let this Agni burn you up.

sanskrit: yat sapatnī sapatnyā amuṣyā varca ādade | adhastād upavādiny asau syād aham uttarāt ||
english: Whatever radiance a rival wife has taken from that woman there — let that one be below as the disparager, while I am above.

sanskrit: ā te badhnāmy oṣadhiṃ sapatnībhyaḥ pracātanīm | yathā te 'sad ayaṃ patiḥ putrāṇāṃ te bhavat pitā ||
english: I bind onto you this herb that drives away rival wives — so that this man may be your husband and become the father of your sons.

sanskrit: yāny ṛṇāny anuvartāny asmin yamasya yena balinā carāmi | idaṃ tad agne anṛṇo bhavāmi- -idaṃ tad agne avadānam astu ||
english: Whatever debts of mine persist in this world — the debts of Yama by whose force I move — of those, O Agni, I become free from debt; of those, O Agni, let this be the clearing.

sanskrit: yās te sapta pravato yā u tisro yās te santi nivato yā abhīvataḥ | arvāvato aṣṭadhā trīṇi rocanā tās te agne saṃmanaso bhavantu jānan yamāya ni vahā kusīdam ||
english: Your seven downward slopes, and also your three, your downward courses, and those that turn toward us — the three luminous regions on this side, eightfold — may all these, O Agni, be of one mind with you. Knowing this, carry the usury down to Yama.

sanskrit: yās ta ūrdhvās tanvo jātavedo yās tiraścīr uta yā anūcīḥ | tābhiṣ ṭvam agne sayujā gṛṇāno jānan yamāya ni vahā kusīdam ||
english: Your upward bodies, O Jātavedas, those that go crosswise and those that go along — yoked together with them, praised, O Agni — knowing this, carry the usury down to Yama.
